get.summary: List the caller's own API tokens.
get.description:
List the caller's own API tokens.

Metadata only: tokens are stored hashed, so the plaintext value is never
returned again after creation. Requires a browser session — an API token may
not enumerate tokens.

start.description: First characters of the token, e.g. `gsf_a1b2c3`.

last_request.description: `null` until the token is first used.

401.description: No authenticated caller could be resolved

403.description: These routes require a signed-in session: a token may not mint or revoke tokens, so a leaked one cannot issue itself successors.

post.summary: Mint a new API token for the caller, carrying the caller's own permissions.
post.description:
Mint a new API token for the caller, carrying the caller's own permissions.

`expires_in_days` is optional — omitting it mints a non-expiring token, which
is what an unattended script usually wants. The response is the only place the
plaintext token ever appears; it is stored hashed and cannot be shown again.
Requires a browser session — a token may not mint another token.

requestBody.description: Omit `expires_in_days` for a token that never expires.

name.description: Label shown in the token list.

201.description: The created token. `token` is the plaintext secret and is returned only here — GSF stores just its hash.

start.description: First characters of the token, e.g. `gsf_a1b2c3`.

last_request.description: `null` until the token is first used.

400.description: `name` is missing, or `expires_in_days` is out of range.

401.description: No authenticated caller could be resolved

403.description: These routes require a signed-in session: a token may not mint or revoke tokens, so a leaked one cannot issue itself successors.

delete.description:
Revoke a token. Deletion is immediate and irreversible — the next request
carrying that token fails to resolve a user and gets a 401. The plugin scopes
the delete to the session user, so `id` can only ever name the caller's own
token; an id belonging to someone else reads back as "not found".

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Id of one of the caller’s own tokens.

200.description: The token is revoked; requests carrying it now fail with 401.

401.description: No authenticated caller could be resolved

403.description: The caller authenticated with an API token — revocation requires a session.

404.description: No such token belongs to the caller.

get.summary: Better Auth's GET surface: session lookup and the SSO callbacks.
get.description:
Better Auth's GET surface: session lookup and the SSO callbacks.

Public by design — sign-in and the callback that completes it must both be
reachable without a session. The plugin's own `/api/auth/api-key/*` routes
are blocked here so `/api/api-tokens` stays the single way to manage tokens.

404.description: `{all}` is not a Better Auth route.

post.summary: Abort the agent run in flight for a conversation the caller owns.
post.description:
Abort the agent run in flight for a conversation the caller owns.

This is what makes the chat UI's Stop button actually stop the run rather than
merely detach the browser from it: an abandoned run keeps the conversation's
slot claimed and the next question is rejected with 409. Cancelling ends the
run without a final answer, so the persisted user turn keeps no assistant
reply. 404 when the conversation does not exist or belongs to someone else.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Conversation whose in-flight run to abort. Must belong to the caller.

401.description: No authenticated caller could be resolved

403.description: The caller lacks the required permission

404.description: Missing/unknown `conversationId`, or it belongs to another user.

502.description: The backend refused the cancel. The upstream status is used when it has one, 502 otherwise; the body is plain text either way.

post.summary: Ask a question and stream the answer back as Server-Sent Events.
post.description:
Ask a question and stream the answer back as Server-Sent Events.

FastAPI emits the SQL plus the formatted answer first (`result`), then —
when that answer has an executed result — generates and persists the
chart/table bubble itself and streams it back as its own `charts` event
before the stream closes. No second request needed from this route or the
browser. Passing `conversation_id` persists the turn and additionally
requires `conversation: ['write']`; the route answers 409 while that
conversation already has a run in flight. Omitting it runs the question
statelessly, with no history and no chart step.

requestBody.description: SQL plus a formatted answer, streamed as SSE. When the answer has an executed result, the backend also generates and persists a chart (or fallback table) and streams it back on this same connection as its own `charts` event — no follow-up call needed. Reuse one `conversation_id` for follow-up turns; an unknown UUID creates a conversation, while an ID owned by another user returns 404. Omitting `conversation_id` runs the question statelessly, with no history and no chart step.

200.description: Server-sent events; the stream ends with `data: [DONE]`

401.description: No authenticated caller could be resolved

403.description: The caller lacks the required permission

409.description: Relayed from the backend: a run is already in flight for this conversation, or the semantic layer has not been compiled yet.

get.summary: Reattach to a chat run already in progress, as a Server-Sent Events stream.
get.description:
Reattach to a chat run already in progress, as a Server-Sent Events stream.

A reloaded or reopened tab uses this to follow a run it did not start. It is a
passive observer: it never submits a question and persists nothing, so a
dropped watch connection has no effect on the run or on what gets saved. 400
without `conversation_id`, 404 when the conversation is not the caller's.

parameters.name: conversation_id
parameters.description: Conversation whose in-flight run to observe. Must belong to the caller.

200.description: Server-sent events; the stream ends with `data: [DONE]`

401.description: No authenticated caller could be resolved

403.description: The caller lacks the required permission

404.description: Unknown conversation, or it belongs to another user.

502.description: The backend refused the watch. The upstream status is used when it has one, 502 otherwise; the body is plain text either way.

put.summary: Turn column profiling on or off instance-wide (admin-only).
put.description:
Turn column profiling on or off instance-wide (admin-only).

Deliberately does NOT trigger a compilation run. The flag is read at the top
of each run, so it applies from the next one onward — flipping it is a change
of policy, not a request to recompile. Operators who want it applied now can
use Reset, which is on the same page.

requestBody.description: Anything other than `true` turns the flag off.

200.description: The stored flag. Takes effect from the next compilation run; this does not trigger one.

put.summary: Turn scheduled semantic compilation on or off instance-wide (admin-only).
put.description:
Turn scheduled semantic compilation on or off instance-wide (admin-only).

Enabling also kicks off a compilation run immediately and starts the ingestion
service's scheduler, so the change takes effect without a restart. That
trigger is best-effort: the setting is still saved if the service is down, and
the scheduler picks the flag up on its next boot.

requestBody.description: Anything other than `true` turns the flag off.

get.description:
Resolve an OIDC issuer's discovery document, admin-only.

The document is fetched server-side and relayed as the endpoints the SSO
registration form needs.

Resolving the endpoints here (instead of letting Better Auth's SSO plugin
auto-discover from the issuer) lets us register providers with
`skipDiscovery: true`. For public IdPs that path requires no `trustedOrigins`
entry, so admins can add any provider without per-provider config.

Gated on sso:manage (admin) — it's an outbound fetch proxy.

ColumnAttribute.description:
A ColumnAttribute of a Term.

``primary_column`` is the HAS_ATTRIBUTE owner and ``referenced_columns``
the SEMANTIC_FK sources; both are absent from the patch response, which
echoes only the fields it wrote.
ColumnAttribute.title: ColumnAttribute

ColumnAttributeExplorationColumn.description:
One Column HAS_ATTRIBUTE/SEMANTIC_FK-linked to a ColumnAttribute.

Same shape as `ColumnExplorationForeignKeyColumn` — enough for a
client to graft it on as a fully expandable Column node.
`relationship_types` mirrors `TermExplorationTable.relationship_types`:
a Column reaching the same attribute via more than one edge type
collects both once grouped.
ColumnAttributeExplorationColumn.title: ColumnAttributeExplorationColumn

ColumnAttributeExplorationDetails.description:
A ColumnAttribute's own owning Term and every linked Column, for
expanding it on the graph.

`term` is `None` only when the attribute has no owning Term (or it's
out of scope). `columns` is one ordered page of *every* Column
HAS_ATTRIBUTE/SEMANTIC_FK-linked to this attribute — not just the
"primary" one whichever expansion grafted this attribute on already
knew about — since a shared attribute (e.g. a common `user_id`-shaped
one) can be linked from many Columns across many Tables at once. See
`fetch_column_attribute_exploration_details`.
ColumnAttributeExplorationDetails.title: ColumnAttributeExplorationDetails

ColumnAttributePatchResponse.description:
``term_certification`` is the owning Term's badge, recomputed on write.

The patch returns it alongside ``data`` so the Terms list can update the
badge without a second request, which is why this needs its own model
rather than the plain ``DataResponse`` envelope.
ColumnAttributePatchResponse.title: ColumnAttributePatchResponse

ColumnExplorationAttribute.description:
The ColumnAttribute HAS_ATTRIBUTE/SEMANTIC_FK-linked to a Column, if any.

`relationship_type` names the relationship kind
(``HAS_ATTRIBUTE`` or ``SEMANTIC_FK``) actually connecting the Column
to this ColumnAttribute — same rationale as `relationship_types` on
`TermExplorationTable`/`ExplorationLink` — so a client can label the
edge the same way it would read in the graph itself, distinguishing a
plain attribute from an FK-shaped one (like `user_id`).
ColumnExplorationAttribute.title: ColumnExplorationAttribute

ColumnExplorationDetails.description:
A Column's own ColumnAttribute, outgoing FOREIGN_KEY target Column,
incoming FOREIGN_KEY source Columns, and referencing Sql queries, for
expanding it on the graph.

`column_attribute`/`foreign_key_column` are `None` for a column with no
ColumnAttribute/no outgoing FK; `referencing_columns` is empty when no
other Column's own FK points at this one (the reverse of
`foreign_key_column`); `sql_queries` is empty for a column no stored
query ever referenced directly — see `fetch_column_exploration_details`.
ColumnExplorationDetails.title: ColumnExplorationDetails

ColumnExplorationForeignKeyColumn.description:
The Column a Column's own outgoing FOREIGN_KEY edge points at, if any.

Carries the target Column's own owning Table/Schema/Database ids/names
(like `ExplorationLinkPathNode` does for a link-path hop) so a client
can graft it onto the graph as a fully expandable Column node — see
`expandColumnNode` in `ExplorationView.tsx`.
ColumnExplorationForeignKeyColumn.title: ColumnExplorationForeignKeyColumn

ColumnRef.description: A column with the catalog path ids needed to navigate to it.
ColumnRef.title: ColumnRef

ColumnSummary.description: One column of a table, ordered by ``ordinal_position``.
ColumnSummary.title: ColumnSummary

ConnectionTestResponse.description: ``schemas`` is empty for connectors that cannot enumerate schemas.
ConnectionTestResponse.title: ConnectionTestResponse

CustomAnalysis.description: A verified SQL example, joined with the text of its ``Sql`` node.
CustomAnalysis.title: CustomAnalysis

DatabaseSummary.description: One catalog database. ``schemas`` is always empty — the tree is lazy.
DatabaseSummary.title: DatabaseSummary

DataExplorationGraph.description: ``{nodes, links}`` for the data layer, in one response.
DataExplorationGraph.title: DataExplorationGraph

DataGraphNode.description:
A table on the data-layer exploration graph.

``relationship_count`` is the table's degree over the whole accessible
edge set, so it does not shrink when ``limit`` truncates the payload.
DataGraphNode.title: DataGraphNode

DescriptionSuggestionResponse.description: ``data`` is null when no description could be suggested.
DescriptionSuggestionResponse.title: DescriptionSuggestionResponse

EntityCoverageCandidate.description: One retrieved semantic candidate, ranked by vector distance.
EntityCoverageCandidate.title: EntityCoverageCandidate

max_distance.description: Maximum L2 vector distance for a candidate to count (lower score = closer match).
max_distance.title: Max Distance

EntityCoverageResult.description:
A 0–1 coverage grade with the candidates it was graded from.

``uncovered_entities`` is only present when the flow was asked for it.
EntityCoverageResult.title: EntityCoverageResult

ExplorationEdge.description:
Two tables connected by a shared SQL query and/or a foreign key.

``queries`` is empty for an edge that exists only because of a foreign
key; ``foreign_keys`` is empty for a SQL-only edge. ``relationship_types``
names the relationship kind(s) behind the edge (``SQL`` and/or
``FOREIGN_KEY``), for labeling the connection in the graph.
ExplorationEdge.title: ExplorationEdge

ExplorationLinkPath.description:
The real ordered hop chain connecting two Terms, e.g. Term1
<-REPRESENTS- Table -CONTAINS-> Column -SEMANTIC_FK-> ColumnAttribute
-PROPERTY_OF-> Term2 — see `fetch_semantic_link_path`. ``hops`` is
ordered from the first term to the second; empty only for a stale/
hand-crafted request naming two terms with no path connecting them.
ExplorationLinkPath.title: ExplorationLinkPath

ExplorationLinkPathHop.description:
One relationship traversed along a term↔term path.

``relationship`` is the underlying type (``REPRESENTS``, ``CONTAINS``,
``HAS_ATTRIBUTE``, ``SEMANTIC_FK`` or ``PROPERTY_OF``).
ExplorationLinkPathHop.title: ExplorationLinkPathHop

ExplorationLinkPathNode.description:
One Term/Table/Column/ColumnAttribute node along an `ExplorationLinkPathHop` chain.

``type`` matches the Exploration graph's own node kinds (``term``,
``table``, ``column``, ``columnAttribute``) so a client can graft/style
this node exactly like any other of that type — see
`fetch_semantic_link_path`. The catalog fields are only ever set for a
``table``/``column`` type node (see ``_enrich_catalog_path_nodes`` in
``gsf/dal/attributes.py``) — the same ids a client needs to expand
either one further, exactly like a Table/Column node grafted anywhere
else in the app, so neither is a dead end just because it came from a
link path instead. ``table_id``/``table_name`` are a ``column`` node's
own owning Table, additionally.
ExplorationLinkPathNode.title: ExplorationLinkPathNode

ExplorationRelatedNode.description: One related node. The catalog path fields are data-layer only.
ExplorationRelatedNode.title: ExplorationRelatedNode

ExplorationRelatedNodes.description: One page of related nodes; ``total`` counts every related node.
ExplorationRelatedNodes.title: ExplorationRelatedNodes

ExportRequest.description: Export scope: empty ``databases`` exports every catalog database.
ExportRequest.title: ExportRequest

ForeignKeyRef.description:
One foreign-key column pair behind an exploration edge.

``source_column`` always names a column on the edge's ``source``. The
sample values are rendered through ``stringify_sample_values`` before
reaching this model, so the types a column stores arrive here as a plain
string list.
ForeignKeyRef.title: ForeignKeyRef

GlobalSearchBreadcrumb.description: One hop in a global-search hit's catalog/semantic path.
GlobalSearchBreadcrumb.title: GlobalSearchBreadcrumb

GlobalSearchItem.description:
One global-search hit: identity plus optional certified/parent path.

``type`` is the entity's label (``Term``, ``Table``, ``ColumnAttribute``, …).
``table_type`` is set on ``Table`` nodes so the client can tell views apart.
GlobalSearchItem.title: GlobalSearchItem

GraphLink.description:
An undirected term↔term link (two terms sharing at least one table).

``relationship_types`` names the relationship kind(s)
(``REPRESENTS``, ``HAS_ATTRIBUTE``, ``SEMANTIC_FK``) connecting either
term to a table they share, for labeling the connection in the graph.
GraphLink.title: GraphLink

IdRef.description: ``{"id": ...}`` — echoed by the delete endpoints to confirm the target.
IdRef.title: IdRef

ModelFormat.description: Serialisation dialect of an exchanged model document.
ModelFormat.title: ModelFormat

NodeUpdateResult.description:
Echo of a catalog node patch: ``{id, ...the properties you sent}``.

``update_node_properties`` builds the body as ``{"id": ..., **{k: props[k]
for k in patch}}``, so only the keys the request actually patched come
back — every one of them is optional here for that reason, and each may be
null when the node has no value for it. The route as a whole answers null
when the patch was empty or the node does not exist.
NodeUpdateResult.title: NodeUpdateResult

PqlAnalysis.description: A verified PQL few-shot. The PQL text is a property, not a child node.
PqlAnalysis.title: PqlAnalysis

PublicConnection.description:
A UI-managed connection with its credentials stripped.

``connection`` is absent from the delete response, which echoes only the
database name it tore down; the list and create reads carry the full
credential-free config.
PublicConnection.title: PublicConnection

SchemasPayload.description: ``/schemas/{db_id}`` — unenveloped; null when the database is missing.
SchemasPayload.title: SchemasPayload

SchemaSummary.description: One schema of a database, with how many tables it holds.
SchemaSummary.title: SchemaSummary

SemanticExplorationGraph.description: ``{nodes, links}`` for the semantic layer, in one response.
SemanticExplorationGraph.title: SemanticExplorationGraph

SemanticGraphNode.description: A term on the semantic-layer exploration graph.
SemanticGraphNode.title: SemanticGraphNode

SqlAttribute.description:
A SqlAttribute with its owning Term and the SQL text behind it.

``zones`` is resolved only by the single-attribute read; ``sql_id`` and
``database_name`` only by the create/update writes.
SqlAttribute.title: SqlAttribute

SqlAttributeExplorationDetails.description:
A SqlAttribute's own Sql query and owning Term, for expanding it on the graph.

Both are `None` only when the attribute itself doesn't exist (or is out
of scope) — see `fetch_sql_attribute_exploration_details`. `sql` alone
can be `None` when the attribute's SQL touches a table outside the
caller's zones even though the attribute/term are visible.
SqlAttributeExplorationDetails.title: SqlAttributeExplorationDetails

SqlAttributeExplorationSql.description: The Sql query node HAS_SQL-linked to a SqlAttribute.
SqlAttributeExplorationSql.title: SqlAttributeExplorationSql

SqlAttributePatchResponse.description: ``term_certification`` is recomputed only when the patch names a term.
SqlAttributePatchResponse.title: SqlAttributePatchResponse

SqlExplorationColumn.description:
One Column the Sql node's own `SQL` edge connects to directly.

Same shape as `ColumnAttributeExplorationColumn` — enough for a client
to graft it on as a fully expandable Column node.
SqlExplorationColumn.title: SqlExplorationColumn

SqlExplorationCustomAnalysis.description: A CustomAnalysis HAS_SQL-linked to the same Sql node as a SqlAttribute.
SqlExplorationCustomAnalysis.title: SqlExplorationCustomAnalysis

SqlExplorationDetails.description:
The CustomAnalysis, Column, Table and SqlAttribute nodes hanging off a Sql node.

`custom_analyses` is empty for the common case of a Sql node with no
CustomAnalysis sharing it; `columns` is every visible Column the Sql
node's own `SQL` edges reach directly; `tables` is every visible Table
the Sql node's own `SQL` edges reach directly; `sql_attributes` is every
visible SqlAttribute this same Sql node backs (the reverse of
`SqlAttributeExplorationDetails.sql`) — see
`fetch_sql_exploration_details`.
SqlExplorationDetails.title: SqlExplorationDetails

SqlExplorationSqlAttribute.description:
A SqlAttribute HAS_SQL-linked to the Sql node, with its owning Term.

`term_id`/`term_name` are `None` only when the SqlAttribute has no
owning Term at all — an out-of-scope owning Term instead drops the
whole row, same as `fetch_sql_attribute_exploration_details`'s own
`term`.
SqlExplorationSqlAttribute.title: SqlExplorationSqlAttribute

SqlExplorationTable.description:
One Table the Sql node's own `SQL` edge connects to directly.

One hop out from the statement along its own `SQL` edge — enough for a
client to graft it on as a fully expandable Table node, same shape as
`SqlExplorationColumn` minus the column-only fields.
SqlExplorationTable.title: SqlExplorationTable

SqlExpressionValidationResult.description: ``/sql-attributes/validate`` — a parse failure is a 422, not ``valid: false``.
SqlExpressionValidationResult.title: SqlExpressionValidationResult

SqlValidationResult.description: ``/custom-analyses/validate`` — a parse failure is a 422, not ``valid: false``.
SqlValidationResult.title: SqlValidationResult

SsoFederationState.description:
The one flag ``PATCH /connections/{database_name}/sso-federation`` sets.

The route deliberately echoes just the flag rather than the connection, so
a caller never has to re-send credentials to toggle it.
SsoFederationState.title: SsoFederationState

TableColumns.description:
A table with one page of its columns.

Every field but ``columns`` is absent from the empty fallback the route
returns when the table (or its schema/database path) is missing.
TableColumns.title: TableColumns

TableExplorationDetails.description: The table-detail modal: its SQL queries and one page of its Terms.
TableExplorationDetails.title: TableExplorationDetails

TableExplorationTerm.description:
A Term linked to a table, with the relationship kind(s) reaching it.

``relationship_types`` names how this term connects to the table —
``REPRESENTS`` directly, and/or ``HAS_ATTRIBUTE``/``SEMANTIC_FK`` via one
of its columns — the same way ``ExplorationEdge``/``GraphLink`` name
theirs, so a client can label the connection the same way it would read
in the graph itself.
TableExplorationTerm.title: TableExplorationTerm

TableSqlQuery.description:
A stored SQL query that references the table.

``sql`` is nullable: unlike the other Sql reads in ``gsf/dal/exploration``
this query has no ``_NON_EMPTY_SQL`` filter, so a Sql node with a null or
blank ``sql_full_query`` reaches the response. Declaring it required would
turn that row into a 500 for the whole table-detail modal.
TableSqlQuery.title: TableSqlQuery

TableSummary.description: One table of a schema, with its column / SQL / Term counts.
TableSummary.title: TableSummary

Term.description: A Term with its certification rollup and resolved zone chips.
Term.title: Term

TermCountEntry.description: ``{term_id, count}`` — one per-term breakdown row. Zeroes are omitted.
TermCountEntry.title: TermCountEntry

TermDetail.description: One Term with the tables that represent it and its related terms.
TermDetail.title: TermDetail

TermExplorationDetails.description: One ordered page of Tables linked to a Term, for expanding it on the graph.
TermExplorationDetails.title: TermExplorationDetails

TermExplorationTable.description:
A Table linked to a term, with the relationship kind(s) reaching it.

The reverse of ``TableExplorationTerm``: ``relationship_types`` names how
this table connects to the term — ``REPRESENTS`` directly, and/or
``HAS_ATTRIBUTE``/``SEMANTIC_FK`` via one of its columns — so a client can
label an expansion edge from either end the same way.
TermExplorationTable.title: TermExplorationTable

TermListItem.description: A Term as it appears in the paged ``/terms`` list.
TermListItem.title: TermListItem

TermsPageResponse.description:
One page of the Terms list with its per-term count breakdowns.

``total`` counts every matching term; the count lists cover only the
terms on this page when a limit was given.
TermsPageResponse.title: TermsPageResponse

TermSummary.description: The three fields every Term projection carries.
TermSummary.title: TermSummary

TermTable.description: A table that REPRESENTS a Term, with its catalog path ids.
TermTable.title: TermTable

Zone.description:
A zone with its catalog data items.

``items`` is absent on the list endpoint, a list of ``ZoneItem`` on the
detail/update endpoints, and a plain list of the ids that were linked on
create.
Zone.title: Zone

ZoneChip.description:
A zone as rendered next to something else it grants access to.

``enabled`` is false for a zone whose ``Zone`` label was swapped for
``disableZone``; those are returned to admins only.
ZoneChip.title: ZoneChip

ZoneItem.description: A catalog node a zone grants access to (a database, schema or table).
ZoneItem.title: ZoneItem
